name: OH-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+21 partisan lean makes this one of the safest Republican House seats
Jordan holds an overwhelming cash advantage (~$4.5M on hand vs ~$3K for the Democrat)
Prediction markets price a Democratic upset near 5%
No public polling and little outside attention to the race
model.rationale: A 21-point Republican district, Jordan's massive financial edge, and market pricing near 95% for Republicans leave no evidence of a competitive contest, so the forecast rests on fundamentals and points to a roughly 20-point Republican margin.
model.watch: Only a dramatic scandal or a late wave of outside spending against Jordan could narrow a race that currently shows no competitive signals.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ohio's 4th District is a deeply Republican seat, and Jim Jordan enters the general election as a heavy favorite after clearing his primary. The district's partisan lean of roughly 21 points Republican, combined with Jordan's national profile and incumbency, frames this as one of the safest Republican House seats on the map. Fundraising underscores the imbalance: Jordan has built a war chest of about $4.5 million, while Democratic nominee Joshua Kolasinski has raised roughly $25,000 and has only about $3,000 on hand. An independent candidate, Tracey Tackett, is also on the ballot but shows no measurable financial footprint.

Prediction markets give Democrats only a small chance of an upset, and no public polling has been conducted in the race. Barring an extraordinary development, Jordan is positioned to win another term by a wide margin.
